import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])

# Group by date and product to get total sales per day per product
daily_sales = df.groupby(['date', 'product'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a line plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=daily_sales, x='date', y='total', hue='product', marker="o")

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.title('Daily Sales Trend by Product')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.legend(title='Product')

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])

# Group by date and product to get total sales per day per product
daily_sales = df.groupby(['date', 'product'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a line plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=daily_sales, x='date', y='total', hue='product', marker="o")

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.title('Daily Sales Trend by Product')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.legend(title='Product')

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
